text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocks(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Shooting(x, y) ::: x shoots at y.
Michael ::: the individual Michael.
Windy ::: the individual Windy.
Peter ::: the individual Peter.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, then x can block y’s shooting.
Taller(Michael, y) for all y ≠ Michael ::: Michael is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: Transitivity of taller relation.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x (Taller(x, y) ∧ ¬Jump(x) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: Michael can block any shooter who does not jump.
¬Blocks(Michael, Windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Anyone who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.
Conclusion:
¬GreatShooter(Windy) ::: Windy is not a great shooter.
